result.title: When Does Physics Beat Data? Data-Efficient Traffic State Estimation with Amortized PINNs
result.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Accepted at the SSTDM workshop, IEEE ICDM 2026
result.summary: Traffic state estimation (TSE) reconstructs traffic density at unmonitored locations from a sparse set of sensors. Data-driven models work well when sensors are dense but degrade sharply as coverage thins. We show that imposing the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards conservation law as a physics-informed prior makes TSE more data-efficient. On four real corridors (NGSIM, I-80, PeMS04, PeMS08), physics-informed estimators generalise to held-out sensors where data-driven models, including classical and deep kriging, overfit the observed ones. On the two shock-rich corridors the effect is a clear crossover: as more sensors are held out, data-driven models collapse while the physics-informed estimator degrades gracefully, leading the no-physics network by about 26-38% at 85-90% held out and the strongest classical kriging by about 10-21% at 90%. A matched smoothness prior does not reproduce the gain, and an extended Kalman filter on the same LWR model is outperformed on the shock corridors, so the advantage comes from how the conservation law is imposed. Finally, one loss-conditional PINN removes the per-corridor loss-weight search, matching a 20-point search at about 5x lower cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究稀疏传感器下的交通状态估计，将 LWR 守恒律作为物理先验加入 PINN，在四条真实道路上验证其对未布点传感器的泛化优于数据驱动方法与 kriging，并给出单损失条件 PINN 以省去逐路段损失权重搜索。
AI.relevance_reason: 交通状态属于远离视觉推理的领域，但其「摊销式推断+结构化物理先验在证据稀疏时的平缓退化」与匹配平滑先验的对照，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据变稀时 latent 状态该由何种结构化先验约束、以及性能交叉点如何评价。
